summary: Full-extraction pass over 10 stored US documents (three USCIS EB-5 statistics PDFs, five USCIS/White House web pages, 8 U.S.C. 1427). program_terms.applies_to: investor; standard amount (petitions filed on or after 15 Mar 2022)
program_terms.location: table 'minimum investment amounts by filing date'
program_terms.quote: On or After 3/15/2022 $1,050,000 $800,000 (includes infrastructure projects) N/A
program_terms.notes: Same amount as the 2022 Act (usa-law-pl117-103-2022). The page says amounts will be adjusted for inflation every five years, the first adjustment effective for petitions filed on or after 1 Jan 2027.

program_terms.applies_to: investor; targeted employment area or infrastructure project (petitions filed on or after 15 Mar 2022)
program_terms.location: table 'minimum investment amounts by filing date'
program_terms.quote: On or After 3/15/2022 $1,050,000 $800,000 (includes infrastructure projects) N/A

program_terms.applies_to: investor; high-employment area (petitions filed before 15 Mar 2022)
program_terms.location: table 'minimum investment amounts by filing date'
program_terms.notes: Same as the standard amount. For petitions filed on or after 15 Mar 2022 the page prints "N/A" for a separate high-employment amount. valid_from follows the existing rows from this table (vacatur of the 2019 rule on 22 Jun 2021).

program_terms.applies_to: each investor: full-time positions for qualifying employees created by the new commercial enterprise
program_terms.quote: must invest the required amount of capital in a new commercial enterprise that will create full-time positions for at least 10 qualifying employees.
program_terms.notes: Page reflects the rules under the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act (page updated 18 Nov 2025); start date not given on the page. Full-time means at least 35 hours a week. In a troubled business the investor may instead maintain jobs.

program_terms.applies_to: regional-center investors: maximum share of the job creation requirement met by indirect jobs
program_terms.quote: Up to 90% of the job creation requirement for regional center investors may be met using indirect jobs.
program_terms.notes: Standalone investors must create the jobs directly. Start date not given on the page.

program_terms.applies_to: share of EB-5 immigrant visas set aside each fiscal year for investors in a rural area
program_terms.notes: Set-asides created by the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act (signed 15 Mar 2022, per the page). Unused set-aside visas stay in the category one more fiscal year, then go to unreserved EB-5 numbers in the third year. Not a cost: a visa allocation rule.

program_terms.applies_to: share of EB-5 immigrant visas set aside each fiscal year for investors in a high unemployment area
program_terms.notes: Set-asides created by the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act (signed 15 Mar 2022, per the page). Unused set-aside visas stay in the category one more fiscal year, then go to unreserved EB-5 numbers in the third year. Not a cost: a visa allocation rule.

program_terms.applies_to: share of EB-5 immigrant visas set aside each fiscal year for investors in a infrastructure project
program_terms.notes: Set-asides created by the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act (signed 15 Mar 2022, per the page). Unused set-aside visas stay in the category one more fiscal year, then go to unreserved EB-5 numbers in the third year. Not a cost: a visa allocation rule.

program_terms.applies_to: investor; standard amount under the 2019 Modernization rule (later vacated)
program_terms.quote: The standard minimum investment amount has increased to $1.8 million (from $1 million) to account for inflation.
program_terms.notes: The page states the rule took effect 21 Nov 2019 and was vacated on 22 Jun 2021 (Behring Regional Center LLC v. Wolf), after which USCIS applied the earlier regulations. valid_to is the day before the vacatur.

program_terms.applies_to: investor; targeted employment area under the 2019 Modernization rule (later vacated)
program_terms.quote: The minimum investment in a TEA has increased to $900,000 (from $500,000) to account for inflation.
program_terms.notes: As for the standard amount: in effect from 21 Nov 2019 until the rule was vacated on 22 Jun 2021.

program_terms.applies_to: each designated regional center, per year (USD 10,000 for some, as directed by the law)
program_terms.quote: USCIS must collect a $20,000 or $10,000 fee, as directed by the new law, for the EB-5 Integrity Fund from each designated regional center.
program_terms.notes: The page does not say which centers pay USD 10,000 (per the 2022 Act: 20 or fewer investors in the preceding fiscal year). valid_from: date of the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act; collection started later (notice of 2 Mar 2023).

program_terms.applies_to: each designated regional center: audited by USCIS at least once every five years
program_terms.quote: we must audit each designated regional center at least once every five years.
program_terms.notes: Requirement added by the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022 (INA 203(b)(5)(E)(vii)). Not a cost: an oversight rule.

program_terms.applies_to: permanent residents (all categories, incl. investors): continuous residence after lawful admission for permanent residence before applying to naturalize
program_terms.quote: has resided continuously, after being lawfully admitted for permanent residence, within the United States for at least five years
program_terms.notes: General naturalization rule, not specific to the programme. The applicant must also have been physically present for "at least half of that time" (words, not recorded as a number) and have lived in the state or USCIS district for at least three months. For EB-5 investors the conditional residence period counts. Edition: United States Code 2023; the rule dates from 1952 as amended (date not recorded as valid_from).

program_terms.applies_to: permanent residents (all categories, incl. investors): continuous residence after lawful admission for permanent residence before applying to naturalize
program_terms.quote: has resided continuously, after being lawfully admitted for permanent residence, within the United States for at least five years
program_terms.notes: General naturalization rule, not specific to the programme. The applicant must also have been physically present for "at least half of that time" (words, not recorded as a number) and have lived in the state or USCIS district for at least three months. For EB-5 investors the conditional residence period counts. Edition: United States Code 2023; the rule dates from 1952 as amended (date not recorded as valid_from).

events.title: USCIS fee schedule restores pre-April 2024 EB-5 filing fees
events.description: USCIS published a new edition of Form G-1055 (Fee Schedule) returning the filing fees for Forms I-526, I-526E, I-829, I-956, I-956F and I-956G to the amounts in force before the 1 April 2024 fee rule, following the court order partially staying the 2024 fee rule. Also announced on usa-uscis-web-eb5-whats-new-2025.
events.quote: On Nov. 14, 2025, we published a new edition of Form G-1055, Fee Schedule. The new edition changed the filing fees for EB-5 related petitions and applications to the pre April 1, 2024, Fee Rule filing fees

events.title: Court certifies class of investors denied over loan-funded investments (Zhang v. USCIS)
events.description: The U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia certified a class of Form I-526 petitioners denied solely because they invested loan proceeds not secured by their own assets, vacated those denials and ordered USCIS to reconsider. USCIS wrote to denied and withdrawn petitioners in May 2019 and appealed on 28 Jan 2019.
events.quote: On Nov. 30, 2018, in the case of Zhang v. USCIS, No. 15-cv-995, the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia certified a class

events.title: Appeals court upholds Zhang v. USCIS ruling; USCIS reopens class members' petitions
events.description: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit affirmed the district court decision on loan-funded EB-5 investments; USCIS said it was reopening and adjudicating class members' Form I-526 petitions consistent with the decision.
events.quote: On Oct. 27, 2020, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit affirmed the district court’s decision.

events.title: Final deadline for unpaid FY2023-FY2025 Integrity Fund fees; non-payers face termination
events.description: USCIS said the FY2025 EB-5 Integrity Fund fee was due from 1 Oct 2024; delinquent FY2023 and FY2024 payments were accepted from 1 Oct to 30 Dec 2024, and USCIS would take steps to terminate any regional center that had not paid all three years by 30 Dec 2024 (the law requires termination 90 days after the fee is due).
events.location: alert 'NOTICE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2025 INTEGRITY FUND PAYMENTS'
events.quote: we will take steps to terminate any regional center that, on or before Dec. 30, 2024, has not paid the required EB-5 Integrity Fund fees for each of FY 2023, FY 2024, and FY 2025.

events.title: Green Card validity extended 48 months for investors with a pending Form I-829
events.description: USCIS extended the validity of conditional Green Cards for petitioners who properly file Form I-829 (or Form I-751) for 48 months beyond the card's expiration date.
events.quote: In January 2023, USCIS extended the validity of Permanent Resident Cards (also known as Green Cards) for petitioners who properly file Form I-751, Petition to Remove Conditions on Residence, or Form I-829

events.title: Deadline for regional center Form I-956 amendments under the Behring settlement lifted
events.description: USCIS said 29 Dec 2022 was no longer the deadline for filing Form I-956 amendments required by the Behring settlement; the deadline is extended until USCIS publishes guidance. The page does not give the date of the announcement; the date is the lifted deadline.
events.quote: Dec. 29, 2022, is no longer the deadline to file Form I-956, Application for Regional Center Designation, amendments, as required by the Behring Settlement.

events.title: Separate fee payments required for EB-5 petitions filed with other forms
events.description: From 1 Sept 2022 USCIS no longer accepts a single combined fee payment when Form I-526 or I-526E is filed together with Forms I-485, I-131 or I-765; combined payments lead to rejection.
events.quote: Beginning Sept. 1, 2022, we will no longer accept a single, combined fee payment when an applicant or petitioner files Form I-526

events.title: USCIS clarifies guidance on deployment of EB-5 investment capital
events.description: USCIS updated the USCIS Policy Manual with clarifying guidance on the initial and further deployment of investment capital under the EB-5 programme.
events.quote: USCIS has updated the USCIS Policy Manual with clarifying guidance on the deployment of investment capital under the EB-5 Immigrant Investor Program.

USCIS web page (updated 18 Nov 2025) on EB-5 requirements: alert on the 14 Nov 2025 Form G-1055 fee schedule restoring pre-April 2024 fees (event added); programme history (1990 creation, 1992 regional center pilot, 15 Mar 2022 Reform and Integrity Act, regional center visas through 30 Sept 2027: already in events from other sources); new commercial enterprise definition (40% expansion test); job creation (10 jobs, 90% indirect for regional centers: added as terms); troubled business (2 years, 20% loss) and full-time (35 hours) definitions; capital definition; minimum investment table (before 15 Mar 2022 USD 1,000,000 / 500,000 / 1,000,000 high-employment; from 15 Mar 2022 USD 1,050,000 / 800,000: pre-2022 standard and TEA terms already in the data, the other three added); five-yearly CPI-U adjustment from 1 Jan 2027 (already in events); TEA definitions (150% unemployment, 20,000 population); visa set-asides 20% rural, 10% high unemployment, 2% infrastructure (added as terms). Not recorded as separate terms: definitional thresholds (40%, 2 years and 20% loss, 35 hours, 150%, 20,000), which define eligibility rather than set a price or quota.

USCIS web page (updated 1 Mar 2023): programme overview (10 jobs, 1990 creation, 1992 Regional Center Program); notice that the 2019 Modernization rule was vacated on 22 Jun 2021 (Behring Regional Center v. Wolf, already in events) with the rule's content (USD 1.8 million / USD 900,000 minimums from 21 Nov 2019: added as terms from this page; priority date retention, TEA reform, I-829 procedure, five-yearly CPI-U adjustment); Zhang v. USCIS class action (certified 30 Nov 2018, appeal 28 Jan 2019, letters May 2019, affirmed 27 Oct 2020: two events added); DHS privacy notice. The 2019 rule's 20,000-population and 150% thresholds are definitions, not recorded.

USCIS 'EB-5 What's New' page (updated 18 Nov 2025), a list of alerts: 14 Nov 2025 G-1055 fee schedule restoring pre-April 2024 fees (event recorded once, from usa-uscis-web-eb5-classification-2025); FY2025 Integrity Fund payments due 1 Oct 2024 and final deadline 30 Dec 2024 for FY2023-2025 with termination of non-payers (event added); regional center audits at least every five years (term added) and use of the Yellow Book standards 'Starting April 23' (year not printed: not recorded as an event); I-956G annual statements due 29 Dec 2023 (routine filing reminder, not recorded); Green Card validity extended 48 months for pending I-829s, Jan 2023 (event added); Behring settlement I-956 amendment deadline of 29 Dec 2022 lifted (event added); Integrity Fund USD 20,000 / 10,000 (term added); separate fee payments from 1 Sept 2022 (event added); Behring v. Mayorkas injunction 24 Jun 2022 (already in events); resumed processing of pre-June 2021 regional-center I-526s (undated: not recorded); notice to I-829 filers under Pub. L. 107-273 (I-829 filed before 2 Nov 2002 on I-526s approved 1 Jan 1995-31 Aug 1998; eligibility criteria, not recorded); 15 Mar 2022 law and program through 30 Sept 2027 (already in events); news item of 24 Jul 2020 on capital deployment guidance (event added). No statistics.

USCIS form page for Form I-140G (updated 10 Dec 2025): form edition 11/19/25; online-only filing after registration on trumpcard.gov; fee USD 15,000 per person (principal, spouse, children). The fee (program_terms) and the form's publication (event) were already in the data; nothing else in scope.

8 U.S.C. 1427 (naturalization requirements), U.S. Code 2023 edition, 3 pages, also the end of 8 U.S.C. 1426 and start of 1428: five years continuous residence after admission as a permanent resident, physical presence for at least half that time, three months in the state or district (5-year residence added as a term for usa-eb5 and usa-gold-card); rules on absences (more than six months / one year break continuity), exceptions for US government and certain employer staff, good moral character, naturalization for extraordinary contributions to national security (at most five a year), amendment history and the expired 2005 subsection (g) (3-year reduction for international events, USD 1,000 premium fee). Only the general residence period concerns the investor programmes; the rest is general naturalization law and out of scope.

White House fact sheet, 19 Sep 2025: Executive Order 14351 creates the Gold Card (launch event already in the data from the order itself); gift amounts USD 1 million individual / USD 2 million corporate (added as terms from this source); gifts deposited into the Treasury; agencies to set application processes and fees; political statements. Japan's USD 550 billion and the EU's USD 600 billion investment commitments are trade pledges unrelated to the programme (out of scope).
